title: Generalized s-d model for Wannier-Mott excitons in layered magnetic semiconductors
authors: Sonu Verma, Bashab Dey, Akashdeep Kamra
abstract: The recent discovery of excitons coupled to the magnetic order, and the consequent strong magneto-optic responses, in some van der Waals magnetic semiconductors has triggered intense activity at the interface of magnetism and semiconductor optics. Here, we present an analytically tractable minimal model that describes magnetic order, electrons, holes, and excitons within a unified framework, thereby capturing a wide range of phenomena. It treats the magnetic order and itinerant carriers to be comprised by distinct electronic orbitals that are mutually coupled via orbital-dependent onsite exchange, similar to the treatment of metallic magnets using an s-d model. Investigating CrSBr bilayer as a case study, we benchmark our model and its predictions against recent experimental and ab-initio results finding good agreement as well as new insights enabled by the model's simplicity. Examining the optical selection rules, we find the conservation of a quantum number formed from a combination of spin and layer pseudospin to be a useful guiding principle, even in noncollinear magnetic configurations. Our analysis finds a series of bright and dark excitonic states in such layered A-type antiferromagnets. The presented framework should be valuable in achieving intuitive understanding of recently discovered excitonic phenomena and guiding the discovery of other excitonic states in layered magnetic semiconductors.
summary: This paper introduces a generalized s-d model to unify the description of magnetism, itinerant carriers, and excitons in layered magnetic semiconductors like $	ext{CrSBr}$. By analyzing the system's response across different magnetic field regimes, the authors predict specific excitonic states and provide a guiding principle based on conserved quantum numbers for understanding these complex magneto-optic effects.
main_problem: To develop a unified, analytically tractable minimal model describing the interplay between magnetic order, itinerant electrons, and excitons in layered magnetic semiconductors.
main_result: The model successfully captures the coupling between magnetic order and excitonic phenomena, providing a framework to understand magneto-optic responses in these materials.
method: The authors employ a generalized s-d model Hamiltonian, reducing it for magnetically ordered states and analyzing the resulting electronic structure and exciton binding energies.
model_or_system: The study focuses on layered van der Waals magnetic semiconductors, using $	ext{CrSBr}$ bilayer as a case study. The model incorporates magnetic order, electron/hole dynamics, and excitons via an extended Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Bright and dark excitonic states, optical selection rules (conservation of a spin/layer pseudospin quantum number), and exciton binding energy.
important_parameters: Magnetic canting angle ($\alpha$), hopping amplitudes ($t_{	au x}, t_{	au y}, t_{	au \perp}$), and onsite exchange couplings.
main_assumptions: The localized-spin operators are replaced by their expectation values for a magnetically ordered state, and the analysis often relies on a two-channel exciton model approximation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the reduced low-energy model for $	ext{CrSBr}$ bilayer. Figure 2 summarizes the field-driven evolution of magnetic order (AFM $	o$ Canted $	o$ FM). Figure 7(b) plots layer probabilities.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the unified Hamiltonian, then analyzing the electronic structure evolution under magnetic field canting using symmetry principles (SRLP), and finally calculating the resulting Wannier-Mott exciton properties and binding energies.
why_interesting: The explicit inclusion of magnetic order into the exciton physics via the s-d model provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding magneto-optics, which bridges condensed matter theory with quantum optics.
